blocks.text: Setting up Notion for program coordinators on Mac

Your Mac is the command center for your programs. Start by installing the official Notion desktop app. This ensures you have access to system-level features and native notifications. Once installed, create a master database for your projects. Use the `/database` command to trigger the block menu. Select Database - Full page to get started.

items: Create a Project Tracker database to manage deadlines.
Add a Status property to track progress using tags like Not Started, In Progress, and Done.
Use a Date property for key milestones.
Link your projects to a secondary database for team members or stakeholders.

blocks.text: Lazur helps you stay in the flow while working in Notion. If you need to find a specific project, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where your project tracker is located. Lazur circles the element on your screen. You can also use Lazur to dictate meeting notes directly into a page. Just hold fn and speak your updates.

Many coordinators fall into the trap of over-engineering their Notion pages. Keep your structure simple at first. Avoid creating too many nested pages that make information hard to find. Use a clear naming convention for your databases. For example, prefix your databases with a tag like Projects or Resources to keep your sidebar organized.
Use the ⌘ P shortcut to open the search bar. This is the fastest way to jump between pages without clicking through your sidebar.

Coordination requires clear communication. Use Notion callouts to highlight important project updates. You can also use the @ mention feature to tag team members in comments. This triggers a notification in their workspace. Always keep your documentation updated to reduce the need for status meetings.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Notion pages directly?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not click buttons or edit files for you. It helps by pointing at items, answering your questions, and dictating text.

faq.question: Does Notion require a specific macOS version?
faq.answer: Yes, the Notion desktop app requires macOS 13 Ventura or later.
